title: V_eta migration coverage ledger
description: One row per did_v1 SOURCE class, from BOTH v1 writers: the NDI production templates (read from NDI-matlab `origin/main`, not a lagging feature branch) AND the vhlab app/calculator classes that appear in real corpora but ship no NDI template (footprint = a bespoke migrator that consumes them). Post-v1 DID intermediate classes (zarr, directory, the `*_observation` leaves, ...) are V_eta TARGETS, not v1 sources, and are excluded.

no_target_recorded.cause: `decided_targets` is empty, so rung 2 has nothing to look for in the built set and rung 3 has nothing to check an emission against. NOT evidence that no target exists
no_target_recorded.why_the_join_moves_none_of_them: a decision citation names a decision LINE, not a per-class target list. The join can say a class is decided; it cannot say WHAT it becomes. Naming a target from it would be inventing one

corpus_rung.why: no corpus report root was supplied (pass --corpus-reports DIR or set V_ETA_CORPUS_REPORTS)

Each report must carry `source_census.by_class` (per v1 SOURCE class) plus `quarantine_count`, `fragment_count`, `reference_integrity.orphan_count` and `silent_loss.empty_required_dependency`.

decided_by_citation.decision: the control of a stimulus presentation is a `logical` covariate `control condition` (XCO:0000099) along the presentation dimension of the stimulus `item` value (data_body plan AMENDMENT 6): true where the presentation was a control. rows.how: KEEPS ITS CLASS -- a block FOLD, not a dissolution. `oneepoch` is the record of a CONCATENATION (ndi.element.oneepoch glues an element's N epochs into one); its only own field, `epoch_ids`, is the comma-joined list of the sources. Everything else arrives by inheritance from `element_epoch`, which V_eta renames to `acquisition_epoch` -- so no class of that name exists to inherit from and the inherited block would trip the strict top-level check (did2:validation:undeclaredBlock). The migrator moves that block's contents onto the `oneepoch` block and drops the shell. Field-by-field, so an unrecognised v1 field surfaces as undeclaredField rather than riding along unvalidated.

It migrates 1 -> 1 with `base.id` PRESERVED, which is load-bearing -- `subject_id` is the most-referenced edge in the corpus and a minted id would dangle every one of them. The did_v1 template declares exactly `local_identifier` and `description`, and V_eta declares exactly those two, so nothing is dropped and nothing is invented. rows.how: NO PASS-1 MIGRATOR, deliberately: the document passes through under its own tombstone (the identity migrator), which is what stops it stranding. CORRECTED 2026-09-25 (#73 item 52): an earlier version of this note said the second pass was RE-ARMED as of 2026-08-18. It was NOT: the signed amendment of that date says 'IS NOT RE-ARMED YET', and resolveValidIntervals.m at 775353d (2026-08-13, the head of both DID-matlab V_eta branches) is still 'DORMANT BY DECISION -- census only; emits nothing', its preserved code being the rejected 1->N shape. THE SIGNED TARGET (TEAM-SIGN-OFF [logical_observation amendment 1], V_eta_logical_observation_plan.md, 2026-08-18): the leaf is `observation + time`, NOT `logical_observation` (retired, #73 item 52), and THE INTERVAL TIMES ARE THE VALUE. One statement per source document carrying an N x 2 array of `time` cells keyed [interval (a bare regular index), endpoint (labels `start`, `end`)], so the pairing is DECLARED rather than positional (T14). WHY THE BOOLEAN ARRAY WAS WITHDRAWN: the v1 class declares four fields (timeref_structt0, t0, timeref_structt1, t1) and NOT ONE IS A BOOLEAN, so a boolean array would have been INVENTED on every migrated document, and for a list of VALID intervals every element of it is true by construction. Each statement is anchored by a `relative_time_reference` via `time_reference_id` (start = t0, duration = t1 - t0, clock de-encoded from clocktypestring), whose `referent_id` names the minted `epoch` DOCUMENT. A batch pass and not a migrator for the same structural reason as resolveSessionAnchors: that document's id exists only after did2.convert.epochMint has minted it corpus-wide, and a single-document migrator holds an epoch STRING it cannot map to a document id.
rows.target_flags: ADDS, NEVER REMOVES. The source document is KEPT under its v1 tombstone (nothing required, `element_id` optional), so a passthrough cannot trip mustBeNonEmpty or undeclaredField. SIGNED: TEAM-SIGN-OFF [logical_observation] 2026-08-12 plus TEAM-SIGN-OFF [logical_observation amendment 1] 2026-08-18, which supersedes the LEAF AND THE VALUE only -- the 2026-08-12 reasoning about `variable` carrying the semantic, about `sequence` being deleted, about transitive inheritance and about the three reading states all stand. `logical_observation` was left with NO CONSUMER (valid_interval was its only one) and is RETIRED, #73 item 52 (2026-09-25); `logical` stays, like every value. `sequence` is DELETED: v1's array-append order is invisible to its only consumer (tuning_response.m:253-256 indexes identifyvalidintervals's RETURN VALUE, and markgarbage.m:178-204 accumulates every row through a set union without indexing by position). OPEN SUB-QUESTION, deliberately not pre-empted: NDI's loadvalidinterval inherits a derived element's validity from its `underlying_element` (markgarbage.m:146-155), and whether V_eta re-derives that at query time or materialises it is a team call -- both remain buildable.

decided_by_citation.decision: jess@walthamdatascience.com / 2026-08-12 -- `validity` and `validity_observation` are replaced by `logical` + `logical_observation`; the semantic moves to `subject_statement.variable`, since a data_type names the KIND of value and not what it is about. `logical` carries ONE field, `value` typed `boolean` with mustBeScalar false -- a bare array, no wrapper cell (`boolean` is impossible as a class name: it is a primitive in the validator's type switch, cache.m:1793; `logical`:`boolean` mirrors the existing `term`:`ontology_term`). `logical_observation` declares no fields. `sequence` is deleted: NDI never reads interval order, because identifyvalidintervals accumulates through interval_add, a set union, and tuning_response.m:256 indexes THAT union rather than the stored array. THE ARRAY IS THE TARGET MODEL -- one statement per source document holding N booleans against a time axis -- and the 1->N decomposition is NOT shipped as an interim: migration WAITS for `axes[]` on `subject_statement` rather than migrating twice, so the pass is dormant by decision. Inheritance walks the whole `derived_from` chain TRANSITIVELY, MATCHING NDI, whose `loadvalidinterval` calls ITSELF on `underlying_element` and so already recurses to any depth; the divergences are the EDGE (V_eta walks `derived_from` in the migrated document graph, NDI walks a runtime object property) and the SCOPE (v1 has no `variable`, so its fallback cannot be per-variable). Inheritance yields the statement WITH ITS ANCHOR, never the interval numbers alone. Three states, a deliberate break from v1: no statement anywhere -> VALID; statements projected -> use them; statements found but none projectable into the caller's frame -> UNKNOWN, NOT VALID (v1 returns the entire requested span, so a clock mismatch reads as "all data good"). Consumers must count inherited statements they could not project. NOT COVERED BY THIS SIGNATURE: the gap semantics between statements (still undefined, still open), the timing of `axes[]`, and any change to ndi.app.markgarbage's v1 reader behaviour.
